source: Compiled from KSPCB industries directory (publicly available via opencity), Citizen Matters Bengaluru reporting, WELL Labs Bengaluru Urban Water Balance Report (Jan 2024), Forward Foundation v State of Karnataka NGT case filings, IISc CES wetlands studies. Each entry below cites the most specific source we have for the pollution claim - the underlying lat/lng is set on the documented industrial cluster's geographic centroid, not a single facility, because the polluting load is cluster-level not point-source.
_note: Bengaluru's industrial pollution sources are clustered in 4 distinct catchments: (1) Vrishabhavathi catchment from Peenya + Yeshwanthpur draining south-west, (2) K&C valley from Whitefield + Mahadevapura draining into Bellandur-Varthur, (3) Dakshina Pinakini from Bommasandra + Electronic City + Jigani draining south-east into Tamil Nadu, (4) Hebbal valley from Yelahanka industrial draining north-east. Marker placement follows industrial-estate centroids per the KSPCB-published boundary maps.

sources.name: Peenya Industrial Area (Phases 1-4)
sources.operator: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB) + Peenya Industries Association
sources.description: One of Asia's largest small-scale industrial estates, spread across four phases in north-west Bengaluru. Hosts ~13,000 units across engineering, electroplating, chemicals, dyeing, machine tools, and metal finishing. KSPCB has flagged the area's electroplating sub-cluster repeatedly for chromium + cyanide discharge into the Vrishabhavathi catchment via the unlined storm drains running south-west from the estate. The cluster predates the Vrishabhavathi STP build-out and structurally pours into the same watershed the V Valley STPs are trying to clean downstream.
sources.source: KSPCB consent-to-operate violations + Citizen Matters Bengaluru reporting + WELL Labs 2024 industrial-effluent section

sources.name: Bommasandra Industrial Area (Phases 1-4)
sources.description: Large multi-phase industrial estate on the southern fringe of BBMP, just inside Anekal taluk. Mix of electronics manufacturing, pharma units, garment, and a Jigani sub-cluster of biomedical-waste incinerators. Effluent reaches the Dakshina Pinakini via Hosur-Road-aligned storm drains and the Begur lake chain. KSPCB monthly reports flag recurring exceedances on heavy metals + COD from the pharma sub-cluster.
sources.source: KSPCB Karnataka annual report + KIADB Bommasandra master plan + Citizen Matters reporting

sources.name: Whitefield - ITPL + EPIP industrial zone
sources.description: Whitefield's Export Promotion Industrial Park (EPIP) + International Tech Park (ITPL) cluster sits at the Varthur-Bellandur watershed edge. The IT-services population the area supports (~3 lakh employees daily) drives a parallel domestic-sewage load on the K&C valley network that the upstream STPs cannot absorb. Direct industrial discharge is comparatively low; the consequential pollution is the apartment-block storm + sewage runoff that bypasses BBMP collection lines and reaches Varthur Lake via the Yamare-Belathur drainage system. Citizen Matters has documented Varthur foam events upstream of the lake at the Belathur outfall.
sources.source: Citizen Matters Bengaluru + Forward Foundation NGT filings on Bellandur-Varthur

sources.name: Electronic City (Phases 1, 2)
sources.description: Bengaluru's earliest dedicated IT/electronics park (1978-onwards). Phase 1 has ~3 lakh daily employees; Phase 2 adds large campuses (Infosys etc.). Self-managed STPs exist but capacity vs actual load is opaque; ELCIA's own published volumes have been challenged in KSPCB filings. Discharge reaches the Dakshina Pinakini headwaters via Begur-Anekal drainage.
sources.source: KEONICS + ELCIA public disclosures + KSPCB CTO violations

sources.name: Yeshwanthpur APMC + warehousing cluster
sources.operator: Karnataka APMC + multiple private warehousing operators
sources.description: Asia's largest wholesale agri-market complex (APMC Yeshwanthpur) plus surrounding cold-chain + warehousing. The runoff is high in organic load and unsegregated solid waste; reaches Vrishabhavathi via the Mathikere/Sankey storm drainage. The pollutant signature is different from Peenya's (organic + biodegradable rather than heavy metals) but the cumulative BOD impact on Vrishabhavathi is meaningful.
sources.source: BBMP storm-water drain audit + Citizen Matters reporting

sources.name: Mahadevapura IT + light industrial belt
sources.description: Includes RMZ Ecospace, Manyata Tech Park spillover, and several apartment-heavy IT campuses on K&C valley's east arm. Like Whitefield the dominant load is parallel-sewerage rather than direct industrial discharge. Drains into Bellandur via the Mahadevapura-Marathahalli-Kadabeesanahalli storm-water chain.
sources.source: BBMP storm-water audit + Forward Foundation NGT filings

sources.name: Jigani Industrial Area
sources.description: Industrial estate in Anekal taluk south of Bommasandra. Hosts Karnataka's largest cluster of biomedical-waste incinerators + pharma manufacturing. The Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facility (CBWTF) is here. Multiple KSPCB closure notices over the years for emissions + effluent violations.
sources.source: KSPCB CBWTF inspection reports + Karnataka State Biomedical Waste Management Authority

sources.name: Mailasandra (V Valley) - dyeing + small industries cluster
sources.operator: BWSSB Mailasandra 75 MLD STP + adjacent private dyeing units
sources.description: Mailasandra is the V Valley STP outfall point on the Vrishabhavathi. Adjacent are dozens of small-scale dyeing units that historically have NOT been on Karnataka's effluent-monitoring radar. The combined load downstream is what gives Vrishabhavathi its colour signature visible from the Outer Ring Road bridge. STP design 75 MLD; documented over-load and intermittent bypass.
sources.source: OpenCity BWSSB STP locations + Citizen Matters Bengaluru

sources.name: Bellandur Amani Kere STP discharge zone
sources.description: The 90 MLD STP that sits at the literal northern edge of Bellandur Lake. Per Forward Foundation's NGT filings the plant has not consistently met output BOD/COD norms; the cumulative untreated load reaching the lake on a peak K&C-valley day is estimated at 400-500 MLD. Phosphate-rich detergent loads from upstream apartment complexes are documented as the proximate cause of the 2015 + 2018 foam-and-fire events.
sources.source: Forward Foundation v State of Karnataka NGT 2018 order + BWSSB STP locations dataset

sources.name: Bidadi Industrial Area
sources.description: Major automotive manufacturing cluster ~30 km west of central Bengaluru (Toyota Kirloskar plus ancillary suppliers). Sits in the Arkavati catchment; effluent discharge - the bulk of which is treated in-house at large unit ETPs - still reaches the Arkavati downstream of TG Halli. Smaller-unit clusters around the main plants have had repeat KSPCB notices on metal-finishing effluent.
sources.source: KIADB Bidadi master plan + KSPCB consent-to-operate listings

sources.name: Yelahanka Industrial Area (incl. SIDDCO)
sources.operator: KIADB + SIDDCO (TN small industries development corporation analogue)
sources.description: Mixed-use industrial belt in north Bengaluru. Some electroplating + metal finishing units. Discharge reaches the Hebbal-valley drainage and onwards to the Dakshina Pinakini headwaters. Yelahanka is also one of the IISc Groundwater Outlook 65-stress wards - the industrial footprint contributes to local aquifer contamination alongside groundwater over-extraction.
sources.source: KSPCB Karnataka + IISc Groundwater Outlook April 2025

sources.name: Hoskote Industrial Area
sources.description: East-of-Bengaluru industrial cluster sitting close to the Bengaluru-Hosakote-Chennai highway. Includes Honda, Bosch and several auto-ancillary plants plus warehouse logistics. Drains into the Hoskote Lake chain which feeds the Dakshina Pinakini via Sulibele.
sources.source: KIADB Hoskote master plan + KSPCB CTO listings

sources.name: K&C Valley secondary STP cluster (218 + 30 + 60 MLD)
sources.description: BWSSB's 218 MLD (pre-Stage IV) + 30 MLD (Stage IV Phase 1) + 60 MLD (later addition) Koramangala-Challaghatta valley STPs all discharge into the Bellandur-Varthur chain. JICA Phase 3 documents the K&C valley generation rate exceeds the secondary-only treatment design; with industrial + apartment domestic loads combined, the residual untreated discharge into the lakes is the proximate driver of the foam events.
sources.source: JICA BWSSB Phase 3 Final Report Tables 4.1 + 4.4 + 7.1.2

sources.name: Byramangala Reservoir downstream textile cluster
sources.description: Byramangala Reservoir (348 ha) is the largest downstream sink of the Vrishabhavathi system. Receives the cumulative discharge of all V valley STPs + Peenya runoff + Mailasandra dyeing units. The reservoir's water quality has been a recurring concern - KSPCB has classified it as a priority polluted water body. Used for irrigation downstream; documented heavy-metals + colour pollution.
sources.source: KSPCB Karnataka annual report + IISc CES Vrishabhavathi catchment study
